case.case_title: Abdul Razak and Another v. Dharmadasa, Chief Inspector of Police, Katugastota and Others
case.source_citation: Sri Lanka Law Reports [1999] 1 Sri LR. S.C. Application No. 877/96 (FR), decided on 17 December 1998

clause.text: Any person detained shall be brought before a judge and cannot be held without legal order.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the detention of the petitioners prior to being produced before the Magistrate was lawful and complied with Article 13(2) of the Constitution.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioners claimed that their detention was unlawful as they were held without a legal order and without being released on bail despite being entitled to bail for non-cognizable offences.
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents argued that the detention was lawful as the petitioners were arrested on a complaint alleging a cognizable offence and were produced before the Magistrate accordingly.
key_facts: Petitioners were detained at the police station from arrest until produced before the Magistrate.
The offences under sections 480 and 484 are non-cognizable and bailable.
The petitioners were not requested to furnish security for bail as required by law.
The Magistrate committed the petitioners to remand custody before later granting bail.
The police informed the Magistrate they would not file a plaint and the matter was referred to mediation.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: Article 13(2) requires that any person detained be brought before a judge and not held without legal authority. Detention without bail or legal order for non-cognizable offences violates this provision.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The court found that the petitioners were detained unlawfully because the offences alleged were non-cognizable and bailable, yet they were not released on bail or given an opportunity to furnish security. Their detention until production before the Magistrate was therefore unlawful under Article 13(2).
principles_established: Detention without legal order or bail for bailable, non-cognizable offences violates Article 13(2).
Police must follow proper procedures for bail and security to avoid unlawful detention.
precedents_cited: Faiz v. Attorney-General and Others (1995) 1 Sri LR 372

outcome.holding: The court held that the detention of the petitioners was unlawful and violated Article 13(2) of the Constitution.
outcome.remedy_or_orders: The respondents were ordered to pay compensation for the unlawful detention.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(2) is central to the court's finding that the petitioners were unlawfully detained without legal order or bail, reinforcing the constitutional protection against arbitrary detention.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The court noted that the petitioners were detained without bail despite the offences being non-cognizable and bailable, and that the police failed to request security, making the detention unlawful under Article 13(2).
